lead.title: UK startup Cerebella is raising a pre-seed for a digital programme tackling menopause-related brain fog
lead.deck: Cerebella Foundations is a self-guided ten-session programme over five weeks (25 to 30 minutes each) combining psychoeducation, CBT-based activities and gamified memory and attention exercises. A three-week proof-of-concept reports gains in verbal memory, attention and sleep; the company is aiming for employer pilots, clinical trials, then clinician recommendation and reimbursement. The size of the pre-seed and the investors are undisclosed.

milestone.title: Withings and Function link daily at-home measurements with more than 160 lab results
milestone.summary: Withings' Body Scan and Body Smart scales and BPM Vision and BPM Connect blood pressure monitors feed Function's app automatically; in return, more than 160 lab results (ApoB, Lp(a), HbA1c, fasting insulin and more) appear in the Withings app. Available immediately to US users.
milestone.why: The French connected-health maker is pairing with a lab-testing platform to move from one-off readings to longitudinal tracking, notably for patients on GLP-1 drugs. Whether the integration reaches Europe is not stated in the source.

brefsIntl.title: Epic launches "Connectors" to link its AI agents to third-party apps
brefsIntl.summary: Epic's agents (Emmie, Art, Penny and those built in Agent Factory) will be able to retrieve data and act inside third-party software; vendor-built Connectors will be listed on the Epic Showroom from March 2027. Worth watching for European hospitals running Epic.

word.definition: Software, often an app, whose therapeutic effect is its main function and which is prescribed like a treatment.

parts.label: Evidence
parts.role: the clinical trial that justifies use and reimbursement

how.t: A team translates a validated therapeutic protocol (for example cognitive behavioural therapy) into a digital programme.
The software is CE-marked as a medical device (class I or IIa for a German DiGA) and tested in a randomised trial.
Once listed in a directory (DiGA in Germany), it is prescribed by the physician and paid for by health insurance.

word.why: VC angle: recurring revenue backed by a payer and a real regulatory moat, but clinical evidence and reimbursement access remain the bottleneck; young companies like Cerebella target underserved needs before aiming for that pathway.
